title: Guardians get Foster Griffin from Nats to earn a rare A+: MLB trade grades
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

Guardians get: Foster Griffin
Nationals get: Will Dion, Josh Hartle, Kendeglys Virguez and outfielder Nick Mitchell

Guardians: A+
Nationals: D+

Griffin was a coup for the Nationals, a guy who learned a lot in three seasons in Japan and turned himself into an All-Star after signing with Washington for one year and just $5.5 million. He was a model of high-level consistency, going 12-3 with a 3.06 ERA and using seven pitches to frustrate opponents, who hit just .226 with a .285 OBP off him.

It’s discouraging that the Nationals, with a low payroll and almost no long-term commitments, didn’t sign him to a long-term contract. Instead, they’re content to take the win here, and from a big-picture standpoint, I get it. They found a low-cost gem in Griffin and spun him off for four prospects they evidently like. They keep building inventory for a better tomorrow, and Griffin is a rental.

Still, the Nats didn’t get anybody who ranked among Keith Law’s top 17 prospects in Cleveland’s system before this season. Lefty Josh Hartle had the highest ranking, at 18th.

For the Guardians, it’s a brilliant move to bolster an area of strength. They now have the kind of rotation that could help them mount a deep playoff run (if they make it to October): AL strikeout leader Gavin Williams, lefty All-Stars Parker Messick and Griffin, and veteran Tanner Bibee, who has a 2.98 ERA in his last 10 starts.

Guardians: C+ / B-
Nationals: C+

The Nationals surprised everyone by being in the thick of the wild-card standings this year. If not for an offense that ranked at or near the top of the league in a slew of categories over the first half, the question of whether to trade Foster Griffin would have required the phrase “to the (specific team)” to even qualify as good faith. Of course they were going to trade him. They signed him to do just that.

Alas, a 3-7 record in the last 10 games before the deadline turned the Nats back into pumpkins, or at least some gourd-human hybrid, and Griffin is off to Cleveland in return for four prospects. The most intriguing of the group is Hartle, who ranks No. 18 on Keith Law’s top 20 Guardians prospects list. None of the rest have kicked up much dust in the ol’ prospect hype factory, so it feels like a quantity-over-quality situation.

Speaking of factories, you may have heard about the pitching one in Cleveland. The Guardians rank eighth in the league in fWAR from their starting pitchers (10.0). With the dearth of impact bats still available — the Nats had one of those, but he’s a Yankee now — they seem to be capitalizing on an existing strength. Griffin has been very good (12-3, 3.06 ERA, 3.5 bWAR), probably deserving of a better grade, given the price. But unless he plans to pull off a mask and reveal that he’s been a Shohei Ohtani clone this whole time, it doesn’t solve the biggest issue in Cleveland. The Guardians need to score more runs.

Oh, and look at that: as I was typing that out, news broke that they’re trading for Nathaniel Lowe. OK, I’ll bump it up.

— Levi Weaver
